Isfahan-Iran.name: Isfahan
Isfahan-Iran.evidence_basis: Safavid imperial capital from 1598 booming to c. 275,000-350,000 in the seventeenth century (Chardin, Tavernier, Floor); catastrophic collapse after the 1722 Afghan siege to c. 50,000-60,000, followed by late-Qajar textile/opium recovery to 76,000 (1870 count), 82,000 (Curzon 1892), and c. 96,000 by 1925 (Bharier 1972).

Tehran-Iran.name: Tehran
Tehran-Iran.evidence_basis: Modest walled town under the Safavids (walled by Tahmasp I in 1553; Della Valle, Chardin) elevated to Qajar capital in 1786; directly anchored in the 1867 Krziz census (~85,000), 1883-84 Najm al-Dawla census (147,256), Bharier (1972: 210,000 in 1900), and 1922-25 municipal counts (~250,000).

Tabriz-Iran.name: Tabriz
Tabriz-Iran.evidence_basis: Initial Safavid capital (1501-1555) of c. 150,000-200,000 (Venetian reports, Floor); devastated by Ottoman wars and catastrophic 1727/1780 earthquakes to c. 50,000-60,000, before rebounding as the Qajar crown-prince seat and Trebizond trade entrepot to 180,000 (Curzon 1892), 200,000 (1900 Bharier), and 212,000 (1925).

Mashhad-Iran.name: Mashhad
Mashhad-Iran.evidence_basis: Premier Shi'i pilgrimage metropolis of Khorasan; boosted by Safavid royal patronage and Nadir Shah's Afsharid capital status (1736-1747), dip after 1871 famine, then surging with Central Asian rail trade to c. 70,000 in Curzon (1892) and 105,000 by 1925 (Issawi 1971, Bharier 1972).

Qazvin-Iran.name: Qazvin
Qazvin-Iran.evidence_basis: Second Safavid imperial capital (1555-1598) peaking near 80,000-100,000 under Tahmasp I (Floor, Hirano in Kondo 2002); contracted sharply after the court moved to Isfahan, stabilizing as a key Tehran-Rasht-Tabriz highway junction at c. 34,000-45,000 (Curzon 1892, Bharier 1972).

Shiraz-Iran.name: Shiraz
Shiraz-Iran.evidence_basis: Provincial capital of Fars flourishing under Imam Quli Khan and as Karim Khan Zand's capital (1760-1794); contracted after Agha Mohammad Khan's conquest and 1853 earthquake, then enumerated at 53,607 in Fasa'i Farsnameh-ye Naseri (1883-84) and reaching c. 75,000 by 1925 (Curzon 1892, Issawi 1971, Bharier 1972).

Rasht-Iran.name: Rasht
Rasht-Iran.evidence_basis: Provincial capital of Gilan and core of Iran's raw-silk export economy; devastated by the 1830-1832 plague before surging with Caspian-Russian trade and silk/rice commerce to 40,000-45,000 (1890) and c. 70,000 by 1925 (Rabino 1917, Issawi 1971, Bharier 1972).

Hamadan-Iran.name: Hamadan
Hamadan-Iran.evidence_basis: Major western Zagros leather, rug, and Baghdad-Tehran transit city; contracted during the 1724-1730 Ottoman occupation and 1871 famine before surging in the late Qajar period (Issawi 1971, Tumanskii, Curzon 1892, Bharier 1972).

Kashan-Iran.name: Kashan
Kashan-Iran.evidence_basis: Premier Safavid silk-velvet, tile, and copperware industrial centre (Chardin, Tavernier, Floor); severely struck by the 1722 Afghan invasion and catastrophic 1778 earthquake before stabilizing at c. 25,000-34,000 under the Qajars (Curzon 1892, Issawi 1971).

Kermanshah-Iran.name: Kermanshah
Kermanshah-Iran.evidence_basis: Fortified western frontier city rebuilt under Qajar prince-governor Mohammad-Ali Mirza Dowlatshah (1806-1821); major Ottoman-Baghdad trade and pilgrimage gateway assessed at 35,000-40,000 in Curzon (1892) and c. 60,000 by 1925 (Issawi 1971, Bharier 1972).

Kerman-Iran.name: Kerman
Kerman-Iran.evidence_basis: Safavid wool/shawl hub devastated by Agha Mohammad Khan's 1794 sack; recovery directly anchored in Abbott (1850: 25,000), Vaziri Jughrafiya-yi Kerman (1874-75: 40,228), Sykes (1894: 48,000-50,000), and 1911 British consular diaries (~50,000) in de Groot (1978).

Yazd-Iran.name: Yazd
Yazd-Iran.evidence_basis: Resilient central-plateau silk, cotton, and henna manufacturing oasis with prominent merchant and Zoroastrian communities; consistently estimated at 35,000-45,000 in Tavernier, Abbott (1850), Curzon (1892), Kondo (2002), and Issawi (1971).

Ardabil-Iran.name: Ardabil
Ardabil-Iran.evidence_basis: Ancestral shrine heartland of the Safavid dynasty peaking in the seventeenth century (Olearius 1637, Floor); severely depopulated after 1722 wars and Russian occupation (Morier c. 4,000-7,000) before Qajar recovery recorded by Curzon (1892) and Bharier (1972).

Babol-Iran.name: Babol
Babol-Iran.evidence_basis: Commercial capital of Qajar Mazandaran (Barforush); rapid early-nineteenth-century Russian trade boom (Fraser 1822), severe 1830-1832 plague contraction, and late-century stabilization at 30,000-40,000 recorded in Issawi (1971), Curzon (1892), and Rabino (1928).

Hormuz-Iran.name: Hormuz
Hormuz-Iran.evidence_basis: Wealthy Portuguese-held Indian Ocean emporium of c. 35,000-40,000 in the sixteenth century (Portuguese chronicles, Floor 2006); suffered precipitous structural collapse after the 1622 Anglo-Safavid conquest shifted trade to Bandar Abbas, leaving a fishing village of c. 1,200 in Lorimer (1908).

Urmia-Iran.name: Urmia
Urmia-Iran.evidence_basis: Afsharid-dominated walled city in a densely cultivated lake plain hosting major Assyrian/Armenian communities and foreign missions (Kondo 2002, Curzon 1892); suffered steep World War I mass displacement before partial recovery by 1925 (Bharier 1972).

Qom-Iran.name: Qom
Qom-Iran.evidence_basis: Major Twelver Shi'i shrine city (Fatima Ma'sumeh) expanded under Safavid royal patronage (Chardin, Floor); heavily depopulated by the 1722 Afghan devastation before Qajar patronage and the 1922 revival of the Qom hawza boosted it to c. 36,500 (Curzon 1892, Bharier 1972).

Arak-Iran.name: Arak
Arak-Iran.evidence_basis: Grid-planned garrison town founded as Soltanabad in 1808 by Yusef Khan Gorji; rapid late-Qajar expansion driven by European export carpet workshops (Ziegler & Co.) documented in Houtum-Schindler (1896), Curzon (1892), and Issawi (1971).

Zanjan-Iran.name: Zanjan
Zanjan-Iran.evidence_basis: Strategic Khamseh corridor city on the Tehran-Tabriz highway; sharply reduced by the 1850 Babi siege and the 1871 famine (Bassett) before expanding to c. 24,000 in 1890 (Curzon 1892, Issawi 1971) and 32,400 by 1925 (Bharier 1972).

Dezful-Iran.name: Dezful
Dezful-Iran.evidence_basis: Leading northern Khuzestan agrarian and indigo-processing city on the Dez River, overtaking plague-stricken Shushtar in the nineteenth century; Curzon (1892) cites over 16,000-20,000, corroborated by Lorimer (1908) and Bharier (1972).

Khoy-Iran.name: Khoy
Khoy-Iran.evidence_basis: Well-fortified northwestern Azerbaijan commercial and cotton-trading city on the Ottoman frontier; documented by Kinneir (1813), Morier, Curzon (1892), and Bharier (1972).

Borujerd-Iran.name: Borujerd
Borujerd-Iran.evidence_basis: Most populous commercial city of northern Lorestan on the Kermanshah-Isfahan trade corridor; nineteenth-century estimates of 15,000-22,000 documented in Rawlinson (1839), Curzon (1892), and Bharier (1972).

Sanandaj-Iran.name: Sanandaj
Sanandaj-Iran.evidence_basis: Founded in 1636-1637 by Soleyman Khan Ardalan as the capital of the Kurdish Ardalan principality; nineteenth-century compact urban core of c. 15,000-22,000 documented in Rawlinson, Curzon (1892), Yamaguchi (in Kondo 2002), and Bharier (1972).

Abadan-Iran.name: Abadan
Abadan-Iran.evidence_basis: Industrial refinery town founded in 1909 by the Anglo-Persian Oil Company on Abadan Island; rapid workforce expansion tracked in Lorimer (1915), Issawi (1971), and APOC Khuzestan employment records.

Shushtar-Iran.name: Shushtar
Shushtar-Iran.evidence_basis: Historic capital of northern Khuzestan on the Karun hydraulic system; devastated by the 1831-1832 plague (losing over half its population per Layard), then partially recovering to 14,000-18,500 in Curzon (1892) and Lorimer (1908).

Maragheh-Iran.name: Maragheh
Maragheh-Iran.evidence_basis: Fertile garden city south of Mount Sahand and former Ilkhanid capital; severely affected by the 1870-1872 Persian famine before rebounding on dried-fruit exports to Russia (Morier, Curzon 1892, Bharier 1972).

Sabzevar-Iran.name: Sabzevar
Sabzevar-Iran.evidence_basis: Western Khorasan Shi'i commercial city on the Great Khorasan road; late-Qajar cotton-export growth to Russian Central Asia documented in Curzon (1892), Issawi (1971), and Bharier (1972).

Bushehr-Iran.name: Bushehr
Bushehr-Iran.evidence_basis: Elevated from a minor fishing village by Nadir Shah's 1736 naval base and Karim Khan Zand's EIC factory; principal Qajar Persian Gulf port and British Residency assessed at 15,000-20,000+ in Curzon (1892), Lorimer (1908), and Floor (2006).

Sari-Iran.name: Sari
Sari-Iran.evidence_basis: Provincial administrative capital of Mazandaran and early Qajar base of Agha Mohammad Khan; hit hard by the 1830-1832 Caspian plague before gradual recovery tracked in Fraser (1822), Curzon (1892), and Rabino (1928).

Jahrom-Iran.name: Jahrom
Jahrom-Iran.evidence_basis: Major southern Fars date-palm, citrus, and textile city on the Shiraz-Lar route; Qajar growth documented in Fasa'i Farsnameh-ye Naseri (1884), Curzon (1892), and Bharier (1972).

Bandar Anzali-Iran.name: Bandar Anzali
Bandar Anzali-Iran.evidence_basis: Caspian lagoon port serving Rasht and Tehran; transformed from a modest fishing anchorage into Iran's foremost northern foreign-trade entrepot by Baku steamships and Lianozov fisheries as recorded in Curzon (1892), Rabino (1917), and Issawi (1971).

Nishapur-Iran.name: Nishapur
Nishapur-Iran.evidence_basis: Khorasan turquoise-mining and cotton hub on the Mashhad highway; ravaged by 1720s Afghan-Uzbek conflicts before gradual Qajar revival under Bayat governors documented in Fraser (1825), Curzon (1892), and Bharier (1972).

Semnan-Iran.name: Semnan
Semnan-Iran.evidence_basis: Principal oasis city on the western Great Khorasan road famous for cotton-weaving and tobacco; Curzon (1892) estimates under 16,000 inhabitants, corroborated by Houtum-Schindler and Bharier (1972).

Khorramshahr-Iran.name: Khorramshahr
Khorramshahr-Iran.evidence_basis: Founded c. 1812 as Mohammerah at the Karun-Shatt al-Arab confluence by Banu Ka'b leaders; boomed as Sheikh Khaz'al's seat and Karun steam-shipping entrepot to 10,000-12,500 in Lorimer (1908) and c. 18,600 by 1925 (Issawi 1971, Bharier 1972).

Najafabad-Iran.name: Najafabad
Najafabad-Iran.evidence_basis: Planned qanat-fed town founded in 1613 under Shah Abbas I by Shaykh Baha'i west of Isfahan; sustained agricultural and artisan growth tracked in Houtum-Schindler (1896), Sakamoto, and Bharier (1972).

Hoveyzeh-Iran.name: Hoveyzeh
Hoveyzeh-Iran.evidence_basis: Safavid capital of the Musha'sha' governors of Arabistan; devastated by the 1831-1832 plague and the 1837 collapse of the Karkheh River dam, shrinking to a small marshland town documented in Layard and Lorimer (1908).

Torbat-e Heydariyeh-Iran.name: Torbat-e Heydariyeh
Torbat-e Heydariyeh-Iran.evidence_basis: Silk, opium, and saffron emporium south of Mashhad expanded rapidly under the Qara'i ruler Ishaq Khan (d. 1816); nineteenth-century population documented in Fraser (1825), Curzon (1892), and Sykes (1902).

Malayer-Iran.name: Malayer
Malayer-Iran.evidence_basis: Planned Qajar town founded c. 1808 as Dowlatabad by Prince Mohammad-Ali Mirza Dowlatshah under Fath-Ali Shah; rapid carpet and viticulture growth documented in Encyclopaedia Iranica, Curzon (1892), and Bharier (1972).

Birjand-Iran.name: Birjand
Birjand-Iran.evidence_basis: Headquarters of the Alam amirs of Qayenat, surpassing Qaen as southern Khorasan's chief saffron, carpet, and caravan hub; late-Qajar scale documented in Goldsmid (1872), Sykes (1902), and Bharier (1972).

Lahijan-Iran.name: Lahijan
Lahijan-Iran.evidence_basis: Historic Kia'i capital of eastern Gilan (Biya-Pish) and silk-reeling hub where young Ismail I sheltered; Qajar silk and early tea cultivation documented in Rabino (1917), Curzon (1892), and Issawi (1971).

Bandar Abbas-Iran.name: Bandar Abbas
Bandar Abbas-Iran.evidence_basis: Established by Shah Abbas I in 1622 after expelling the Portuguese from Hormuz; peak Safavid VOC/EIC trade analysed by Floor (2006), later declining under Omani lease before reaching c. 10,000 cold-weather inhabitants in Lorimer (1908).

Masjed Soleyman-Iran.name: Masjed Soleyman
Masjed Soleyman-Iran.evidence_basis: Company oilfield town founded immediately after the May 1908 D'Arcy Concession gusher at Maidan-i-Naftun; Bakhtiari and migrant worker camp growth documented in Lorimer (1915), Issawi (1971), and APOC Khuzestan records.

Lar-Iran.name: Lar
Lar-Iran.evidence_basis: Seat of the semi-autonomous kings of Lar annexed by Shah Abbas I in 1601 and major caravan junction on the Shiraz-Bandar Abbas road (Tavernier, Chardin); later Qajar stagnation recorded in Fasa'i (1884) and Curzon (1892).

Quchan-Iran.name: Quchan
Quchan-Iran.evidence_basis: Za'faranlu Kurdish frontier capital on the Ashgabat-Mashhad trade road; grew to c. 15,000 by 1890 (Curzon 1892) before catastrophic earthquakes in 1893 and 1895 destroyed Old Quchan and forced relocation 12 km east (Sykes 1902, Bharier 1972).

Bojnurd-Iran.name: Bojnurd
Bojnurd-Iran.evidence_basis: Fortified Shadlu Kurdish frontier town resettled under Shah Abbas I to guard northern Khorasan against Turkmen incursions; Qajar town size documented in Fraser (1825), Curzon (1892), and Bharier (1972).

Kazerun-Iran.name: Kazerun
Kazerun-Iran.evidence_basis: Principal caravan staging town on the Bushehr-Shiraz mountain trade artery and tobacco/opium depot; assessed from Fasa'i Farsnameh-ye Naseri (1884), Curzon (1892), and Lorimer (1908).

Behbahan-Iran.name: Behbahan
Behbahan-Iran.evidence_basis: Chief walled town of Kuhgiluyeh linking Fars and Khuzestan; regional trade and craft workforce documented in Fasa'i Farsnameh-ye Naseri (1884), Curzon (1892), and Lorimer (1908).

Ahvaz-Iran.name: Ahvaz
Ahvaz-Iran.evidence_basis: Small mud-brick river settlement beside ancient rapids until the opening of Karun steam navigation in 1888 and APOC logistics; assessed from Curzon (1892), Lorimer Gazetteer (1908), and Issawi (1971).

Bam-Iran.name: Bam
Bam-Iran.evidence_basis: Fortified Kerman-Baluchestan gateway; recovered after the 1794 Qajar capture of Lotf Ali Khan Zand to 8,000-9,000 in 1870 (Eastern Persia), 13,000 in 1894 (Sykes), and 14,000 in 1903 consular diaries cited in de Groot (1978).

Nahavand-Iran.name: Nahavand
Nahavand-Iran.evidence_basis: Well-watered agricultural city of western Hamadan/Lorestan borderlands; Ottoman-Safavid garrison history and late-Qajar market growth assessed from Rawlinson (1839), Curzon (1892), and Bharier (1972).

Shahrud-Iran.name: Shahrud
Shahrud-Iran.evidence_basis: Commercial crossroads town linking the Great Khorasan road with Astarabad and Bandar-e Gaz, eclipsing medieval Bastam during the Qajar period (Fraser 1825, Curzon 1892, Bharier 1972).

Shahreza-Iran.name: Shahreza
Shahreza-Iran.evidence_basis: Major caravan and ceramic-craft station (Qomsheh) south of Isfahan on the Shiraz highway; Safavid and Qajar scale documented in Chardin, Curzon (1892), and Bharier (1972).

Gorgan-Iran.name: Gorgan
Gorgan-Iran.evidence_basis: Ancestral Qajar stronghold of Astarabad affected by nineteenth-century plague outbreaks and Yomut Turkmen frontier instability; Curzon (1892) estimates c. 8,000 inhabitants prior to early-twentieth-century cotton-trade recovery (Rabino 1928).

Khorramabad-Iran.name: Khorramabad
Khorramabad-Iran.evidence_basis: Stronghold of Lorestan beneath Falak-ol-Aflak castle with a large seasonally transhumant Lur hinterland; sedentary urban core estimated at 5,000-10,000 by Rawlinson (1839), Layard, and Curzon (1892), growing under early-1920s pacification.

Bandar Lengeh-Iran.name: Bandar Lengeh
Bandar Lengeh-Iran.evidence_basis: Qasimi Arab-Persian entrepot and pearl-trading port that surged in the nineteenth century (10,000-15,000 in Curzon 1892 and Lorimer 1908) before contracting after 1899 Belgian customs tariffs diverted trade to Dubai.

Amol-Iran.name: Amol
Amol-Iran.evidence_basis: Historic Haraz bridge town in Mazandaran reduced by nineteenth-century epidemics and earthquakes; Curzon (1892) explicitly cites c. 8,000 inhabitants, corroborated by Rabino (1928) and Bharier (1972).

Kashmar-Iran.name: Kashmar
Kashmar-Iran.evidence_basis: Irrigated viticulture, silk, and rug hub of Torshiz in central Khorasan; late-Qajar expansion tracked in Curzon (1892), Sykes (1902), and Bharier (1972).

Damghan-Iran.name: Damghan
Damghan-Iran.evidence_basis: Historic Qumis city on the Great Khorasan road devastated during the 1723-1729 Afghan wars; gradual Qajar recovery documented in Fraser (1825), Curzon (1892), and Bharier (1972).

Golpayegan-Iran.name: Golpayegan
Golpayegan-Iran.evidence_basis: Fertile plateau town between Isfahan and Soltanabad with strong woodwork and grain guilds; Safavid and Qajar scale documented in Chardin, Houtum-Schindler (1896), and Bharier (1972).

Zabol-Iran.name: Zabol
Zabol-Iran.evidence_basis: Built c. 1869 as Nasratabad by Qajar governor Mir Alam Khan (Hashmat al-Molk) to anchor Persian control over Sistan; rapid administrative and British/Russian consular growth recorded in Goldsmid (1872), Sykes (1902), and Bharier (1972).

Rafsanjan-Iran.name: Rafsanjan
Rafsanjan-Iran.evidence_basis: Commercial oasis centre (Bahramabad) expanding rapidly on Qajar cotton and pistachio exports; directly documented in Eastern Persia (1870: >5,000), Preece (1892: 8,000), and Gleadowe-Newcomen (1905: 9,000) cited in de Groot (1978).

Shahr-e Kord-Iran.name: Shahr-e Kord
Shahr-e Kord-Iran.evidence_basis: Chaharmahal upland market centre (Dehkord) serving the Bakhtiari tribal confederacy southwest of Isfahan; nineteenth-century expansion documented in Layard, Curzon (1892), and Bharier (1972).

Fasa-Iran.name: Fasa
Fasa-Iran.evidence_basis: Fertile eastern Fars agricultural centre on the Shiraz-Darab corridor; boluk settlement and town scale recorded in Fasa'i Farsnameh-ye Naseri (1884) and Curzon (1892).

Mahabad-Iran.name: Mahabad
Mahabad-Iran.evidence_basis: Administrative centre of the Mukri Kurdish emirate south of Lake Urmia; late-Qajar market growth and World War I frontier disruption documented in Curzon (1892) and Bharier (1972).

Saveh-Iran.name: Saveh
Saveh-Iran.evidence_basis: Historic pomegranate-growing walled town southwest of Tehran; reduced after eighteenth-century Afghan-Zand disruptions and assessed at c. 8,000-10,000 in Houtum-Schindler (1896), Curzon (1892), and Bharier (1972).

Tuyserkan-Iran.name: Tuyserkan
Tuyserkan-Iran.evidence_basis: Highland walnut-growing and felt-weaving town on the southern flank of Mount Alvand; Qajar provincial seat assessed from Rawlinson (1839), Curzon (1892), and Bharier (1972).

Ferdows-Iran.name: Ferdows
Ferdows-Iran.evidence_basis: Historic Quhistan silk and caravan city (Tun) flourishing in the Safavid period before eastern Khorasan trade shifts under the Qajars; assessed from Goldsmid (1872), Sykes (1902), and Bharier (1972).

Fuman-Iran.name: Fuman
Fuman-Iran.evidence_basis: Former capital of western Gilan (Biya-Pas) under the Ishaqvand rulers prior to Shah Abbas I's 1592 annexation and Rasht's rise; later Qajar rice-market scale recorded in Rabino (1917).

Marand-Iran.name: Marand
Marand-Iran.evidence_basis: Orchard oasis on the Tabriz-Julfa trade artery benefiting from the 1916 Russian-built Julfa-Tabriz railway branch; assessed from Morier, Curzon (1892), and Bharier (1972).

Sirjan-Iran.name: Sirjan
Sirjan-Iran.evidence_basis: Developed as Saidabad from the early nineteenth century into the focal commercial town of Sirjan district (24,300 district population in Vaziri 1875); cotton, rug, and pistachio trade analysed in de Groot (1978) and Sykes (1902).

Estahban-Iran.name: Estahban
Estahban-Iran.evidence_basis: Dry-farmed fig, saffron, and textile town of eastern Fars; late-Qajar urban households documented in Fasa'i Farsnameh-ye Naseri (1884) and Bharier (1972).

Ardakan-Iran.name: Ardakan
Ardakan-Iran.evidence_basis: Qanat-irrigated oasis town northwest of Yazd engaged in cotton, henna, and sesame-oil processing; assessed from Yazd provincial monographs (Kondo 2002), Abbott (1850), and Bharier (1972).

Ahar-Iran.name: Ahar
Ahar-Iran.evidence_basis: Administrative seat of Qaradagh in eastern Azerbaijan with Safavid shrine complex of Shaykh Shihab al-Din Ahari; late-Qajar market growth reflected in Curzon (1892) and Bharier (1972).

Langarud-Iran.name: Langarud
Langarud-Iran.evidence_basis: Eastern Gilan river port, silk-spinning town, and Nadir Shah Caspian shipyard site; nineteenth-century commercial growth tracked in Rabino (1917) and Bharier (1972).

Gonabad-Iran.name: Gonabad
Gonabad-Iran.evidence_basis: Ancient qanat-irrigated oasis of southern Khorasan and Nematollahi Sufi centre (Bidokht/Juy-mand); Qajar urban-oasis population assessed from Goldsmid (1872), Curzon (1892), and Bharier (1972).

Salmas-Iran.name: Salmas
Salmas-Iran.evidence_basis: Fertile plain town (Dilman) north of Lake Urmia with mixed Azeri, Kurdish, Armenian, and Assyrian populace; severe World War I frontier devastation reflected in consular reports and Bharier (1972).

Khansar-Iran.name: Khansar
Khansar-Iran.evidence_basis: Narrow mountain-valley orchard and clerical town northwest of Isfahan; nineteenth-century household estimates documented in Houtum-Schindler (1896) and Curzon (1892).

Neyriz-Iran.name: Neyriz
Neyriz-Iran.evidence_basis: Eastern Fars town near Lake Bakhtegan noted for steelwork and figs; suffered severe upheaval during the 1850 and 1853 Babi conflicts before recovering as recorded in Fasa'i Farsnameh-ye Naseri (1884) and Curzon (1892).

Qaen-Iran.name: Qaen
Qaen-Iran.evidence_basis: Historic capital of Quhistan renowned for saffron cultivation, gradually eclipsed politically by Birjand in the Qajar era; late-nineteenth-century size recorded in Goldsmid (1872) and Sykes (1902).

Minab-Iran.name: Minab
Minab-Iran.evidence_basis: Lush irrigated date-palm and citrus oasis east of Bandar Abbas provisioning the Hormuz strait ports; documented in Floor (2006) and Lorimer Gazetteer (1908).

Tabas-Iran.name: Tabas
Tabas-Iran.evidence_basis: Walled date-palm and citrus desert oasis linking Yazd and Khorasan under hereditary Arab-Persian amirs; Qajar scale documented in Curzon (1892) and Sykes (1902).

Ramhormoz-Iran.name: Ramhormoz
Ramhormoz-Iran.evidence_basis: Eastern Khuzestan foothills market town between Ahvaz and Behbahan; explicitly estimated at 8,000 inhabitants in 1900 by Bharier (1972, p. 54) and documented in Lorimer Gazetteer (1908).

Saqqez-Iran.name: Saqqez
Saqqez-Iran.evidence_basis: Northern Kurdistan commercial market on the Sanandaj-Tabriz highland route; Qajar growth documented in Curzon (1892) and Bharier (1972).

Darab-Iran.name: Darab
Darab-Iran.evidence_basis: Citrus, tobacco, and cotton oasis in southeastern Fars; settled town population and boluk agriculture documented in Fasa'i Farsnameh-ye Naseri (1884) and Curzon (1892).

Sarab-Iran.name: Sarab
Sarab-Iran.evidence_basis: Highland grain and wool-rug market town between Tabriz and Ardabil; Qajar population assessed from Morier, Curzon (1892), and Bharier (1972).

Bijar-Iran.name: Bijar
Bijar-Iran.evidence_basis: Administrative seat of Garrus renowned for heavy-weave Qajar carpets; late-nineteenth-century expansion and severe World War I Russian-Ottoman occupation famine shock assessed from Curzon (1892) and Bharier (1972).

Torbat-e Jam-Iran.name: Torbat-e Jam
Torbat-e Jam-Iran.evidence_basis: Shrine town of Shaykh Ahmad-e Jam on the Mashhad-Herat caravan road; Qajar border recovery documented in Curzon (1892) and Sykes (1902).

Maku-Iran.name: Maku
Maku-Iran.evidence_basis: Cliff-sheltered capital of the autonomous Bayat Kurdish-Turkic khanate guarding the extreme northwestern Ottoman-Russian border; Qajar town size recorded in Curzon (1892) and Minorsky.

Abadeh-Iran.name: Abadeh
Abadeh-Iran.evidence_basis: Walled caravan and Indo-European telegraph station on the Shiraz-Isfahan highway documented in Fasa'i Farsnameh-ye Naseri (1884), Curzon (1892), and Bharier (1972) early-twentieth-century provincial town series.

Miyaneh-Iran.name: Miyaneh
Miyaneh-Iran.evidence_basis: Qezel Ozan bridge and caravan staging town on the main Qazvin-Tabriz royal road; travelogue and Qajar district estimates in Morier, Curzon (1892), and Bharier (1972).

Nain-Iran.name: Nain
Nain-Iran.evidence_basis: Desert-margin oasis famous for fine camel-wool cloak (aba) weaving on the Isfahan-Yazd caravan road; documented in Abbott (1850), Houtum-Schindler (1896), and Curzon (1892).

Mahallat-Iran.name: Mahallat
Mahallat-Iran.evidence_basis: Highland oasis town between Qom and Golpayegan serving as the ancestral Qajar seat of the Nizari Ismaili Agha Khans; documented in Houtum-Schindler (1896) and Bharier (1972).

Behshahr-Iran.name: Behshahr
Behshahr-Iran.evidence_basis: Founded as Ashraf in 1612 by Shah Abbas I as a Safavid Caspian winter court (Della Valle, Herbert); decayed sharply in the eighteenth century before late-Qajar agricultural recovery recorded by Rabino (1928) and Curzon (1892).

Taft-Iran.name: Taft
Taft-Iran.evidence_basis: Shir Kuh foothill garden town and pomegranate/felt-making centre southwest of Yazd with Sufi shrine of Shah Nimatallah; assessed from Abbott (1850) and Kondo (2002).

Ardestan-Iran.name: Ardestan
Ardestan-Iran.evidence_basis: Ancient desert-margin oasis on the Kashan-Yazd caravan road; Safavid and Qajar scale assessed from Chardin, Houtum-Schindler (1896), and Issawi (1971) central-plateau gazetteer notes.

Astara-Iran.name: Astara
Astara-Iran.evidence_basis: Talysh Caspian roadstead partitioned by the 1828 Treaty of Turkmenchay; late-Qajar Russian transit customs growth documented in Curzon (1892), Rabino (1917), and Issawi (1971).

Khomeyn-Iran.name: Khomeyn
Khomeyn-Iran.evidence_basis: Agricultural and rug-weaving market town of Kamareh between Golpayegan and Soltanabad; late-Qajar scale assessed from Houtum-Schindler (1896) and Bharier (1972).

Zarand-Iran.name: Zarand
Zarand-Iran.evidence_basis: Agricultural and carpet-weaving qasabeh northwest of Kerman city; central town assessed within the 18,600-person Zarand district recorded in Vaziri Jughrafiya-yi Kerman (1875) via de Groot (1978).

Kangavar-Iran.name: Kangavar
Kangavar-Iran.evidence_basis: Caravan and agricultural market town between Hamadan and Kermanshah built around the ancient Anahita terrace; Qajar estimates in Rawlinson (1839) and Curzon (1892).

Varamin-Iran.name: Varamin
Varamin-Iran.evidence_basis: Irrigated grain-basket town southeast of Tehran eclipsed administratively by the capital's growth after 1786; late-Qajar agrarian recovery recorded in Houtum-Schindler (1896) and Curzon (1892).

Asadabad-Iran.name: Asadabad
Asadabad-Iran.evidence_basis: Fertile Zagros pass town west of Mount Alvand on the Hamadan-Kermanshah pilgrimage highway; documented in Curzon (1892) route surveys and Bharier (1972).

Tonekabon-Iran.name: Tonekabon
Tonekabon-Iran.evidence_basis: Western Mazandaran citrus and rice coastal district centre seat of the Sepahdar-e Tonekaboni estates; Qajar scale documented in Rabino (1928) and Bharier (1972).

Aligudarz-Iran.name: Aligudarz
Aligudarz-Iran.evidence_basis: Eastern Lorestan and Bakhtiari Chahar Lang agricultural market centre on the Borujerd-Isfahan upland corridor; Qajar sedentary expansion assessed from Layard, Schindler (1896), and Bharier (1972).

Firuzabad-Iran.name: Firuzabad
Firuzabad-Iran.evidence_basis: Southern Fars valley town and seasonal hub for the Qashqai tribal confederacy; documented in Fasa'i Farsnameh-ye Naseri (1884) and Curzon (1892).

Khaf-Iran.name: Khaf
Khaf-Iran.evidence_basis: Windmill-powered grain and Sunni-Persian frontier oasis on the Khorasan-Herat corridor; Qajar population assessed from Goldsmid (1872), Curzon (1892), and Sykes (1902).

Damavand-Iran.name: Damavand
Damavand-Iran.evidence_basis: Alborz mountain orchard town and administrative centre east of Tehran; Qajar district scale documented in Houtum-Schindler (1896) and Curzon (1892).

Shahr-e Babak-Iran.name: Shahr-e Babak
Shahr-e Babak-Iran.evidence_basis: Western Kerman plateau town bordering Fars with 80 bazaar shops recorded by Preece (1892) inside a 16,300-person district in Vaziri (1875), cited in de Groot (1978).

Bafq-Iran.name: Bafq
Bafq-Iran.evidence_basis: Date-palm oasis town between Yazd and Kerman; Qajar household scale assessed from Abbott (1850), Vaziri Jughrafiya-yi Kerman (1875), and Sykes (1902).

Natanz-Iran.name: Natanz
Natanz-Iran.evidence_basis: Karkas mountain valley oasis and Safavid royal hunting retreat between Kashan and Isfahan; scale documented in Chardin, Houtum-Schindler (1896), and Curzon (1892).

Ravar-Iran.name: Ravar
Ravar-Iran.evidence_basis: Northern Kerman Lut-margin oasis renowned for fine Qajar carpet weaving (~100 looms by 1900); district and town scale documented in Vaziri (1875) and Sykes (1902) via de Groot (1978).

Ilam-Iran.name: Ilam
Ilam-Iran.evidence_basis: Summer administrative seat (Deh Bala/Hosseinabad) of the semi-autonomous Feyli Lur Valis of Posht-e Kuh; Qajar fortress and bazaar growth documented in Rawlinson (1839), de Morgan (1895), and Lorimer (1908).

Qasr-e Shirin-Iran.name: Qasr-e Shirin
Qasr-e Shirin-Iran.evidence_basis: Western frontier customs station and pilgrimage quarantine post on the Kermanshah-Baghdad highway; Qajar border settlement growth recorded in Curzon (1892) and British consular trade reports (Issawi 1971).

Bandar-e Gaz-Iran.name: Bandar-e Gaz
Bandar-e Gaz-Iran.evidence_basis: Southeastern Caspian steamship roadstead developed from c. 1840 as the maritime outlet for Astarabad and Khorasan cotton exports; documented in Curzon (1892), Rabino (1928), and Issawi (1971).

Zahedan-Iran.name: Zahedan
Zahedan-Iran.evidence_basis: Created in 1916-1918 as Duzdab at the British-Indian Nushki-Duzdab military railhead during World War I; rapid early customs and Indian-merchant boom documented in British Baluchestan trade reports and Bharier (1972).

Mahan-Iran.name: Mahan
Mahan-Iran.evidence_basis: Garden oasis and shrine town of Shah Nimatallah Vali southeast of Kerman; late-nineteenth-century estimates reconcile Vaziri (1875: 1,500 core) and Euan Smith (1870s: 5,000 with orchards) analysed in de Groot (1978).

Saravan-Iran.name: Saravan
Saravan-Iran.evidence_basis: Eastern Baluchestan date-palm oasis (Shastun/Dizak) near the Goldsmid frontier; late-Qajar tribal-settled population assessed from Goldsmid (1872) and Sykes (1902).

Bampur-Iran.name: Bampur
Bampur-Iran.evidence_basis: Historic citadel and Qajar governor's seat in Persian Baluchestan; garrison and oasis population documented in Pottinger (1816), Goldsmid Sistan Commission (1872), and Sykes (1902).

Chabahar-Iran.name: Chabahar
Chabahar-Iran.evidence_basis: Makran oceanic port on the Gulf of Oman held intermittently by Omani rulers before 1872 Qajar reassertion and Indo-European telegraph station installation; assessed from Goldsmid (1872) and Lorimer (1908).

Iranshahr-Iran.name: Iranshahr
Iranshahr-Iran.evidence_basis: Historic Baluchestan oasis town of Pahra/Fahraj on the Bampur River basin; Qajar tribal-administrative population assessed from Goldsmid (1872) and Sykes (1902).

Karaj-Iran.name: Karaj
Karaj-Iran.evidence_basis: Remained a modest agricultural village and royal Qajar estate (Solaymaniyeh Palace) west of Tehran throughout the Safavid-Qajar period, growing only to c. 4,000 by 1925 prior to Pahlavi industrialization (Bharier 1972, Curzon 1892).
